summary_en: The Margaya sets out the everyday occasions on which greed-rooted minds arise. They include seven of the ten unwholesome courses of action, and a long list of ordinary pleasures and cares: drinking, gambling, bribery, music, dance, perfume, fine clothes, tasty food, sport, earning and guarding wealth, courtship, affection between spouses, raising children and arranging their marriages, and pleasure trips; for ordinary people living apart from the teaching, it concludes, most minds from waking to sleep are greed-rooted. It then draws the line by motive: the same act (cooking, eating, dressing, earning, feeding animals) is not unwholesome when it is done from faith, kindness, compassion or practical wisdom (to relieve hunger, keep off cold and insects, avoid contempt), and it is greed-rooted when it is done for taste, beauty, attraction, display or amusement. The Pradeepika extract for this concept gives only the formal list of the eight greed-rooted minds with Sinhala glosses, which shows the three conditions that distinguish them: feeling, wrong view and prompting.

sinhala_explanation.heading: ලෝභමූල සිත් අට සහ ඒවා වෙන් කරන කරුණු (ප්‍රදීපිකාව)
sinhala_explanation.text: ප්‍රදීපිකාව මෙම කොටසේ ලෝභමූල සිත් අට සිංහල අර්ථ සමග ලැයිස්තුගත කරයි [C005-P:L27–L42]. ඒවා එකිනෙකින් වෙන් වන්නේ කරුණු තුනකිනි [C005-P:L12]: (1) වේදනාව — සොමනස්ස සහගත ('සැප වේදනා සහිත') හෝ උපෙක්ඛා සහගත ('මැදහත් වේදනා සහිත') වීම [C005-P:L28] [C005-P:L36]; (2) දිට්ඨිය — වැරදි දැකීම සමග යෙදුන (දිට්ඨිගත සම්පයුත්ත) හෝ නොයෙදුන (දිට්ඨිගත විප්පයුත්ත) වීම [C005-P:L28] [C005-P:L32]; (3) සංඛාරය — මෙහෙයීමක් නැති (අසංඛාරික) හෝ මෙහෙයීමක් ඇති (සසංඛාරික) වීම [C005-P:L28] [C005-P:L30]. පළමු සිත් හතර සොමනස්ස සහගත වන අතර [C005-P:L27–L34], පස්වැනි සිට අටවැනි දක්වා උපෙක්ඛා සහගත වේ [C005-P:L35–L42].

sinhala_explanation.heading: ලෝභමූල සිතින් කෙරෙන අකුසල කර්මපථ (මාර්ගය)
sinhala_explanation.text: අදත්තාදානය, කාමමිථ්‍යාචාරය, මුසාවාදය, පිසුණාවාචා, සම්ඵප්පලාපය, අභිධ්‍යාව සහ මිථ්‍යාදෘෂ්ටිය යන අකුශල කර්මපථ හත කෙරෙන්නේ ලෝභමූල සිත්වලිනි [C005-M:L3].

sinhala_explanation.heading: එදිනෙදා ජීවිතයේ ලෝභමූල සිත් ඇතිවන අවස්ථා (මාර්ගය)
sinhala_explanation.text: සුරාපානය, සූදුව, අල්ලස් ගැනීම හා දීම, රස විඳීමට නැටීම හා නැටුම් බැලීම, වීණා ආදිය වාදනය කිරීම හා ඇසීම, ගී කීම හා ඇසීම, ආස්වාදය පිණිස සුවඳ ගැල්වීම, ලස්සන ඇඳුම් පැළඳුම් හැඳීම, මිහිරි ආහාර පාන, ලස්සන දේ බැලීම, ක්‍රීඩා කිරීම හා බැලීම, ධනය උපයා ගැනීම, ආරක්ෂා කිරීම, ප්‍රිය වස්තූන් සඳහා ධනය වියදම් කිරීම, ඇඳුම්, ගෙවල්, රථ වැනි ප්‍රිය වස්තූන් පිළියෙළ කර පරිභෝග කිරීම යන අවස්ථාවලදී බොහෝ සෙයින් ඇතිවන්නේ ලෝභමූල සිත්ය [C005-M:L5]. තරුණ තරුණියන් එකිනෙකා දැකීමේදී, කතා කිරීමේදී, ගනුදෙනු කිරීමේදී; අඹුසැමියන් එකිනෙකා දැකීමේදී, ප්‍රිය කතා කිරීමේදී; බිරිඳට හා දරුවන්ට ලස්සන ඇඳුම් පැළඳුම් සැපයීමේදී; විනෝද ගමන් යාමේදී; දරුවන් පෝෂණය කිරීමේදී, සුරතල් කිරීමේදී, ඔවුන්ට ආවාහ විවාහ කර දීමේදී ද බොහෝ කොට ඇතිවන්නේ ලෝභමූල සිත්ය [C005-M:L7]. ධර්මයෙන් ඈත්ව වසන සාමාන්‍ය ජනයාට නින්දට යන තුරු දවස මුළුල්ලේ ඇතිවන සිත්වලින් වැඩි කොටස ලෝභමූල සිත් බව කිව යුතු බව මාර්ගය කියයි [C005-M:L7].

sinhala_explanation.heading: එකම ක්‍රියාව, වෙනස් අරමුණ: ධනය, ආහාර, ඇඳුම් (මාර්ගය)
sinhala_explanation.text: ශ්‍රද්ධාව, මෛත්‍රිය, කරුණාව පෙරදැරි කරගෙන ධනය සපයන අයට ඒවායේදී අකුසල් සිත් ඇති නොවේ; ප්‍රයෝජනය සලකමින් නුවණ පෙරදැරි කරගෙන ධනය සපයන, රකින, වියදම් කරන, ඇඳුම් ආහාර සපයන, හඳින, කන බොන අයට ද අකුසල් සිත් ඇති නොවේ [C005-M:L9]. රසය අපේක්ෂාවෙන් හෝ ශරීරය ලස්සන කර ගැනීමේ අපේක්ෂාවෙන් ආහාර පිළියෙළ කරන්නාට හා වළඳන්නාට ඇතිවන්නේ ලෝභමූල සිත්ය [C005-M:L11]; සාගින්න සන්සිඳවීම, ජීවිතය පවත්වා ගැනීම අපේක්ෂාවෙන් ආහාර පිළියෙළ කරන්නාට ඇතිවන්නේ අකුසල් සිත් නොවේ [C005-M:L13]. ලස්සන වීමේ, අනුන්ගේ සිත් ගැනීමේ, උසස් කෙනකු ලෙස පෙනී සිටීමේ අපේක්ෂාවෙන් ඇඳුම් පිළියෙළ කිරීමේදී හා හැඳීමේදී ලෝභමූල සිත් ඇතිවේ [C005-M:L15]; දකින්නන් පිළිකුල් කරන තැන් වසා ගැනීමට, සීතලෙන්, උෂ්ණයෙන්, මැසි මදුරුවන්ගෙන් ආරක්ෂා වීමට ඇඳුම් හඳින්නාට අකුසල් සිත් ඇති නොවේ [C005-M:L17]. ඇඳුම ලස්සන නැති නිසා අනුන් කරන අවමානයෙන් මිදීමේ අපේක්ෂාවෙන් ලස්සන හෝ වටිනා ඇඳුමක් පිළියෙළ කිරීමේදී හා හැඳීමේදී ද අකුසල් සිත් ඇති නොවේ [C005-M:L19].

sinhala_explanation.heading: සතුන්ට හා ළමුන්ට කෑම දීම, ලස්සන සතුන් ඇති කිරීම (මාර්ගය)
sinhala_explanation.text: කන සැටි බලා විනෝද වීම පිණිස සතුන්ට හෝ කුඩා ළමුන්ට කෑම දීමේදී ඇතිවන්නේ ලෝභමූල සිත්ය; සතුන්ට අනුග්‍රහයක් වශයෙන් කෑම දෙන කල්හි ඇතිවන්නේ කුසල් සිත්ය [C005-M:L21]. ලස්සන සතුන් දැක අල්ලා ගැනීමේදී ද, ලස්සන බලනු පිණිස ඔවුන් පෝෂණය කිරීමේදී ද ඇතිවන්නේ ලෝභමූල සිත්ය [C005-M:L23].

key_terms.note: Seven of the ten are done with greed-rooted minds [C005-M:L3].

key_terms.en: taking what is not given, theft

key_terms.note: Motives under which ordinary acts are not unwholesome [C005-M:L9].

key_terms.en: accompanied by joy / by neutral feeling
key_terms.note: The Pradeepika glosses these as 'සැප වේදනා සහිත' and 'මැදහත් වේදනා සහිත' [C005-P:L28] [C005-P:L36].

key_terms.en: joined with / not joined with wrong view

human_interpretation_en.heading: Most of an ordinary day
human_interpretation_en.text: The Margaya is frank that wanting runs through the ordinary texture of life: dressing up, a good meal, music, games, falling for someone, spoiling one's children, planning their weddings, a trip away. It does not call these crimes. It observes that, for most people, most of a day is moved by liking and reaching. It is a description of how much of life runs on wanting, not a list of sins.

human_interpretation_en.heading: It is the why, not the what
human_interpretation_en.text: The same pot of rice, the same shirt, the same salary can come from quite different places. Cooking to satisfy hunger is one thing and cooking for the pleasure of the taste is another. Dressing to keep warm, to be decent, or even to avoid being looked down on is one thing, and dressing to be admired or to seem superior is another. Earning money out of care for others, or with a clear sense of what is useful, is one thing, and earning to possess is another. The outward act can look identical. What differs is the inner aim.

human_interpretation_en.heading: Watching someone eat
human_interpretation_en.text: One small example says a lot. Feeding an animal or a small child because you enjoy watching them eat is counted as a kind of wanting, the pleasure being yours. Feeding the animal for its own sake is counted as good. The same gesture can be about the one who gives or about the one who receives.

does_not_transfer: 'Attachment to family is toxic.' The source says that caring for spouses and children is mostly driven by wanting, but in this extract it does not tell anyone to stop, and it says nothing against family life as such. A film must not frame devoted parents as greedy.
'Only intentions matter.' The source still names particular actions (theft, lying, misconduct) as courses of harm carried out through wanting. It does not dissolve everything into motive.
'Minimalism' or 'self-denial is virtue.' The source explicitly allows good or even valuable clothes worn to avoid contempt, and wealth earned and spent wisely. It does not preach deprivation.
'Art and sport are sinful.' Music, dance and games appear because of the enjoying mind, not because the arts are condemned. A film about artists must not imply otherwise.

story_seeds.seed: A wedding caterer's kitchen at full stretch, and the same cooks eating their own late meal after the event.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: Dishes plated for display and tasted again and again; arguments over presentation; guests queuing; then, in the small hours, the cooks eating plain leftovers standing up, hungry and tired.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: It is the same food with two aims: for taste and display on one side, to quiet hunger on the other. The Margaya draws exactly this line [C005-M:L11] [C005-M:L13].
story_seeds.setting_type: A reception hall kitchen or catering yard in a town
story_seeds.risk: Setting up the cooks as 'virtuous' and the guests as 'greedy'. The film should follow the cooks' craft and working lives.

story_seeds.seed: A small-town tailor in the weeks before the New Year season.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: Customers explaining what they want and why: a festival outfit to impress, school uniforms, a decent shirt for a job interview, a dress to wear to a relative's house where one fears being looked down on.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: The Margaya separates dressing to attract or to look superior from dressing for cover and protection, and from dressing well to escape others' contempt [C005-M:L15–L19].
story_seeds.setting_type: A tailoring shop on a market street
story_seeds.risk: Probing people's motives on camera is intrusive, and poverty can be shown as virtue. Customers must speak in their own words and must not be sorted into good and bad.

story_seeds.seed: A person who feeds stray dogs every evening, and the passers-by who feed the same dogs for fun.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: The regular feeder's routine: bowls, names, checking wounds. Children or visitors tossing food to watch the dogs scramble. The dogs themselves.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: The Margaya contrasts feeding animals to enjoy watching them eat with feeding them as a kindness [C005-M:L21].
story_seeds.setting_type: A bus stand, a temple compound or a fish-landing site where stray animals gather
story_seeds.risk: Sentimentality, and judging the casual passers-by. Nobody should be shamed on camera.

story_seeds.seed: A couple's pre-wedding photo shoot, with families negotiating in the background.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: The photographer directing poses; the couple's shy delight; parents discussing gold, guests and arrangements; the moment of choosing which pictures to keep.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: Courtship, loving talk and arranging a child's marriage are the Margaya's own examples of occasions for greed-rooted minds [C005-M:L7]. The film can show this attachment without needing to judge it.
story_seeds.setting_type: A scenic spot used for wedding photography, and a family home
story_seeds.risk: The source's classification could feel insulting to the couple. The doctrine must stay underneath, and the film must be about them, not about 'greed'.

story_seeds.seed: An ornamental fish and bird shop, and the families who come to choose a pet.
story_seeds.what_camera_could_observe: Children pressing faces to tanks; debates over colours; the shopkeeper's care routines; a bird being chosen and carried home.
story_seeds.why_it_fits: Catching or keeping beautiful animals in order to look at them is listed as an occasion of greed [C005-M:L23], and it can sit beside the real care that some keepers give.
story_seeds.setting_type: A pet shop on a town high street
story_seeds.risk: It could turn into an animal-welfare lecture, or shame children. The keeper's own relationship with the animals should lead.

cross_source_notes: The two extracts cover different material. The Pradeepika's extract for this concept holds only the formal list of the eight greed-rooted minds with Sinhala glosses [C005-P:L27–L42]; its extract header treats 'occasions' as the three distinguishing conditions of feeling, view and prompting [C005-P:L12]. The Margaya gives concrete life situations [C005-M:L3–L23]. The Pradeepika's own concrete material (conditions and examples) sits in the next extract (C006).
The Margaya's seven courses of action done through greed [C005-M:L3] match the seven that the Pradeepika lists in C006 [C006-P:L54].

The Pradeepika glosses 'somanassa' as 'සැප වේදනා' (pleasant feeling) [C005-P:L28], where the Margaya elsewhere keeps 'සෝමනස්ස' (mental joy). In the compendium of feelings (C032) the Pradeepika separates bodily pleasure (sukha) from mental joy (somanassa), so this gloss is loose.
The terminology registers differ: the Pradeepika uses Pali forms (දිට්ඨිගත සම්පයුත්ත, අසංඛාරික), while the Margaya uses Sanskritised Sinhala (දෘෂ්ටිගත සම්ප්‍රයුක්ත, අකුශල කර්මපථ).
uncertainties: C005-P:L40 glosses the seventh mind (upekkhā, diṭṭhigata vippayutta, asaṅkhārika) as 'මෙහෙයීමක් ඇති සිත' (prompted), although asaṅkhārika means unprompted. On the pattern of the other entries it should read 'නැති'. This is a typographical or OCR error and was recorded, not corrected.
The Pradeepika extract assigned to this concept contains no material on 'occasions' in the life-situation sense, so that part of the concept rests on the Margaya alone.
The Margaya's claim that most of an ordinary person's daily minds are greed-rooted [C005-M:L7] is the author's general statement. It is not quantified.

Several Margaya lines say that an act done for need or wisdom is 'not unwholesome' [C005-M:L9] [C005-M:L13] [C005-M:L17] [C005-M:L19] without saying what kind of mind it is instead, whereas feeding animals kindly is explicitly called wholesome [C005-M:L21]. What the other cases are needs an expert check.

The ruling that wearing valuable clothes to escape contempt is not unwholesome [C005-M:L19] is notable (one might expect conceit or wanting to be involved). An expert should check it against other commentaries before any film leans on it.
